Suit is one for recovery of damages of Rs.25,00,000/- with current and future interest at the rate of 18% per annum.

O.S. No.556/2025 2. Case of the plaintiff's in brief is as hereunder:-
The plaintiff is resident of Bengaluru and he hails from a respectable family and he held himself in very high esteem with his relatives and society and he is also serving people in society and has very good reputation and fame among the friends and relatives.

It is stated that the defendant was married with one Mr. Noorullah Shariff,
who is relative of plaintiff and there is family dispute between the defendant and Mr.
Noorullah Shariff.
The plaintiff did not participate in their marriage and nearly contacted defendant and as well as family members of Noorullah Shariff.

Such being the matter, the defendant foisted a false complaint before J.J. Nagar Police Station on 07.06.2023 against her husband and family members and in the said complaint, the defendant has alleged that the plaintiff instigated her husband Noorullah Shariff to treat the defendant in cruel manner and instigated her husband to abuse her in filthy language and she further alleged that it was the plaintiff who O.S. No.556/2025 instigated her husband to assault the defendant and at the instigation of plaintiff, her husband assaulted the defendant on various days.

It is further stated that based on her complaint the jurisdictional police registered FIR against the plaintiff and the Musthaq Ahmed vs Misba C on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72608965/

When the said fact of registration of FIR came to the knowledge of his relatives and friends, they started suspecting the roll of plaintiff in the family affairs of defendant.

The allegation and words used by the defendant in her complaint contains highly defamatory, derogatory allegations against the plaintiff,
levelling several baseless and false allegations knowing fully well that they are untrue,
unfounded and only with a dishonest and willful intention of harming the reputation,
goodwill and name and fame of the plaintiff, the alleged complaint is filed.
3. It is further stated that the allegations made in the complaint has lowered the dignity, morality and integrity O.S. No.556/2025 of the plaintiff in the eye of society and relatives.

The plaintiff every morning visits Masjid for prayer and there also, his friends and relatives started avoiding him,
extending excuses, refusing to talk or move with him.

Whenever his son visited the mosque along with plaintiff, the relatives of the plaintiff maintained distance, because of which the plaintiff was humiliated in various ways by his friends and relatives and he had to take the wrath of social stigma,
wherever he went along with his family members.

It is stated that the jurisdictional police after investigation found that the allegation made by the defendant is without proof and they filed B report against the plaintiff in the said criminal proceedings.
All the allegations made by the defendant in her complaint is malicious propaganda and it has been carried by the defendant knowing fully well.
The same are untrue, false, baseless and unfounded.

Even thereafter, the defendant did not stop her illegal act and again she foisted a false petition against the plaintiff and filed Misc. Pet.
O.S. 4.
The said fact of filing the complaint came to the knowledge of the plaintiff in the month of July 2024, when he appeared in the said case before the Court.

It is stated that the complaint filed before the jurisdictional police and the complaint filed before the Court has destroyed the hard earned reputation, goodwill, name and fame of the plaintiff and because of this, many of his relatives have avoided the plaintiff and the plaintiff was subjected to humiliation, mental torture and agony.

Thus according to the plaintiff, the allegations made in Crl. Misc.197/2023 and in the complaint filed before police are made only with the malafide intention of lowering the dignity of the plaintiff and this has damaged the image of the plaintiff and his reputation in the society and hence the defendant is liable to pay Rs.25,00,000/- as damages for the harm suffered by the defendant and hence the suit.
5. Despite of service of summons, the defendant remained absent and hence is placed exparte.

sentences.text: In support of his evidence P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P.1 which is the copy of the complaint filed by the defendant before J.J. Nagar Police Station dated 07.06.2023 wherein she has stated that she was married to Mr. Noorullah Shariff on 21.01.2022 and she led marital life with her husband for a period of 5 months and thereafter, her husband and her mother-in-law Aseena Taj and her father-in-law i.e. the plaintiff herein and brother-in-law one Naheemulla Shariff picked up quarrels on trivial issues and subjected her to physical and mental cruelty and they instigated her husband to assault her and has sought to initiate action them.

Based on the complaint as per Ex.P.2 FIR is registered against the family members of husband including the plaintiff herein for the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 504 of IPC in Cr. No.100/2023.
14.

Ex.P.3 is the charge sheet which shows the Investigating Officer on completion of investigation has arrived at a conclusion that the accused have committed the O.S. No.556/2025 offences punishable under Section 498A and 504 of IPC and submitted charge sheet.
However, the charge sheet shows it is filed only as against the husband, mother-in-law and brother-in-law of the defendant.

But the plaintiff herein who was shown as accused No.2 is dropped from the charge sheet on the ground that, during the course of investigation there were no supporting evidence to establish guilt against the plaintiff.
Ex.P.4 is copy of the legal notice issued by the plaintiff to the defendant calling upon her to pay damages of Rs.25,00,000/- for the false allegations made against him in Cr. No.100/2023.
Ex.P.6 is the returned postal cover which shows notice has returned unserved.

Ex.P.7 is the copy of the petition in Crl. Misc. No.197/2023 which shows the defendant herein has filed the said petition under Sec.12 of the Protection of Women from the Domastic Violence Act, 2005 wherein she has made various allegations against the respondents No.1 to 5 including the plaintiff.

So the evidence of P.W.1 and the documents produced by him shows the plaintiff is seeking relief on the basis of the allegations made by the defendant before the police and on the ground that a false complaint was filed against him as per Ex.P.1 and she has also made baseless allegations against him in Crl. Misc. as per Ex.P.7 and it is made only with a malafide intention of lowering the dignity of the plaintiff and this has damaged the image of the plaintiff and his reputation in the society.

So, these documents shows the plaintiff herein is dropped from the criminal proceedings and the criminal miscellaneous petition under the provisions of Domestic Violence Act is still pending for adjudication.

16. Further the plaintiff in order to corroborate his claim got examined two witnesses as P.W.2 and 3 and they have in their evidence categorically supported the version of P.W.1 and have deposed that the plaintiff and defendant are O.S. No.556/2025 the relatives of these witnesses and the defendant had filed complaint on 07.06.2023 by stating that the plaintiff instigated Mr. Noorullah to treat the defendant in cruel manner and instigated him to use abusive language and at his instigation, the husband of the defendant assaulted her and based on the complaint Cr. No.100/2023 was registered against the plaintiff and his family members.

It is stated that when these facts came to the Musthaq Ahmed vs Misba C on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72608965/
6 knowledge of these witnesses, they stopped talking with the plaintiff and kept distance and suspected that the plaintiff spoiled the marital life of defendant and decided to keep the plaintiff out of relationship and stopped inviting him to any function.

After few months they came to know that the police filed B report against the plaintiff and his family members and that all the allegations made by the defendant were false and hence, the complaint was filed by the defendant only with an intention to damage the reputation, good will of the plaintiff and now these witnesses have good respect to the plaintiff.
O.S. No.556/2025 17.
At this point of time, it is necessary to note that the defendant has remained exparte.

So by this,
the oral evidence of P.W.1 to 3 and the documents relied upon by him have remained unchallenged and unrebutted.

The present suit is one for damages and in a suit of present nature the onus is upon the plaintiff to establish before the Court that, the statements that were made by the defendant were annoying and has lowered his dignity and reputation in the eye of society.

18. Hence at this point of time it is considered necessary to refer to the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in case of Ram Jethmalani V/s. Subramaniam Swami reported in 2006 AIR (Delhi)
300 wherein it is observed that:
defamation is a public communication which tends to injure the reputation of another.

sentences.text: What statements are defamatory and a span of defences varies from jurisdiction to jurisdiction but there is common agreement in all O.S. No.556/2025 jurisdictions that statements that are unflattering, annoying, irksome, embarrassing or hurt one's feelings are not actionable.
Common elements in in all jurisdictions is the potential to injure the reputation.

So the allegations made in the complaint though is annoying or embarrassing or hurt in the feelings of the plaintiff, the said statements are not actionable and it does not attract the definition of term defamation.
19.

sentences.text: The present suit is filed based on the statement made in the complaint i.e. Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.7 which is the petition filed under the provision of Domestic Violence Act, which according to the plaintiff is defamatory.

On going through the statements and averments made in the petition, it nowhere attracts the term "defamation" as defined by Hon'ble Apex Court in the judgment referred supra and the allegations made in the complaint though is annoying or embarrassing or hurt the feelings of the plaintiff, the said statements are not actionable and it does not attract the definition of term defamation.

So admittedly the criminal O.S. No.556/2025 miscellaneous petition is still pending for adjudication and though the defendant No.2 is dropped from the criminal proceedings,
it is also still pending for adjudication.
So just because, criminal law is set into action based on the complaint filed by the defendant, that does not confer a right upon the plaintiff to bring a suit for defamation.
Further on analysis of the averments made in the complaint it nowhere attracts the definition of the term defamation.

Hence, the plaintiff has failed to establish that the statements made in the police complaint or in the petition are defamatory and in view of pendency of the criminal case and also the criminal miscellaneous petition, in which the plaintiff is a party, it would be too premature to hold that the statements made therein are derogatory.
Hence, the plaintiff is not entitled for the relief claimed.
In view of the reasons assigned so far, this Court proceeds to answer aforesaid points No.1 and 2 in the Negative.

O.S. No.556/2025 21. POINT NO.3 :: In view of findings on points No.1 and 2, this proceeds to pass the following;
ORDER Suit of the plaintiff is dismissed.
Plaintiff shall bear the cost of the suit.
Draw decree accordingly.
